title: Why Were Rainy Nights So DEADLY for Ancient Humans?
title_alternatives: The Hidden Danger of Sleeping in the RAIN
How Ancient Humans Survived a Night of RAIN
Why Ancient Humans Feared Gentle RAIN
The Rainy Night That Could KILL a Hunter
description:
Rain sounds cozy from a modern bed. For most of human history it was one of the most dangerous nights there was. Why sleep makes you lose heat without noticing, why wet beats cold, the flood that comes from rain you never saw, and the five rules ancient people used to survive, from 200,000-year-old grass beds to fires that never died.

This video is history and science, not medical or survival advice.

Sources:
- Wadley et al. (2020). Fire and grass-bedding construction 200 thousand years ago at Border Cave. Science.
- Wadley et al. (2011). Middle Stone Age bedding construction at Sibudu. Science.
- Nadel et al. (2004). Stone Age hut in Israel yields world's oldest evidence of bedding. PNAS.
- Frontiers in Physiology (2017). Sleep and thermoregulation (review).
- Wilderness & Environmental Medicine (2015). Wet clothing removal or a vapor barrier.
- US National Weather Service flash-flood guidance.
